content_structure.introduction: Hook: data-driven companies 23x more likely to acquire customers. Define the jump from predictive to prescriptive to decision intelligence. Preview: tech stack, implementation, use cases, governance.
content_structure.section_1: Analytics maturity model: descriptive → diagnostic → predictive → prescriptive → autonomous. Where most enterprises sit today and what the jump to decision intelligence requires.
content_structure.section_2: Tech stack: data layer (Databricks, Snowflake), ML layer (AutoML, custom models), decision layer (Dataiku, SageMaker), visualization (Looker, Power BI), feedback loops.
content_structure.section_3: 6-step implementation: define decision target, audit data sources, build baseline model, run pilot with decision group, measure accuracy vs. human baseline, scale with governance.
content_structure.section_4: Use cases with ROI: demand forecasting (retail −28% inventory waste), churn prediction (SaaS +19% retention), credit risk (fintech −31% default rate), predictive maintenance (manufacturing −40% downtime).
content_structure.section_5: Governance: data lineage, model drift monitoring, bias auditing (fairness metrics), regulatory compliance (EU AI Act), explainable AI requirements.
content_structure.conclusion: 3-step roadmap to decision intelligence maturity. CTA: Download the Decision Intelligence Readiness Assessment.
content_structure.faq_section: Q1: How is predictive analytics different from business intelligence? Q2: Do we need a data science team to use decision intelligence? Q3: How do we handle model drift? Q4: What's the EU AI Act compliance requirement for predictive models?

content_structure.introduction: Hook: 68% of regulated industries blocked from cloud AI by data sovereignty. Define the self-hosted AI imperative. Preview: platform comparison, architecture, security hardening, compliance.
content_structure.section_1: Why regulated industries must self-host: GDPR data residency, HIPAA PHI requirements, EU AI Act high-risk classifications, government data classification rules.
content_structure.section_2: Platform comparison: Ollama (developer-friendly, macOS/Linux), LM Studio (GUI-based), vLLM (production-scale serving), HuggingFace Inference Endpoints (private cloud). Model options: Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma.
content_structure.section_3: Architecture patterns: single GPU workstation (SMB), multi-GPU server (mid-enterprise), Kubernetes cluster with vLLM (enterprise), air-gapped deployment (government).
content_structure.section_4: Security hardening: network isolation, mTLS API access, role-based access control, prompt injection defenses, audit logging, vulnerability scanning.
content_structure.section_5: TCO comparison: cloud API costs vs. on-premise hardware + ops at 50K, 500K, 5M requests/month. Break-even analysis by tier.
content_structure.conclusion: 5-step self-hosted AI deployment checklist. CTA: Download the Self-Hosted AI Security Hardening Guide.
